main_text.p: 2. Si virtus agens patientis excedat resistentiam agentis. Actio enim fit à valentiori.
3. Si resistentia agentis nullo externo juvetur.
4. Si agens ita vicinum sit patienti, ut hoc in illud agere possit. Non tamen omne patiens tantum patitur, quantum agens agit. Nam idem movens eadem vi vario motu saepius movet diversa[?].
Monstru.Naturæ porrò peccatum dicitur MONSTRUM, quod est vitium naturæ deficientis ob aliquod impedimentum.

p.i: Vitium hoc Naturæ fit 1. A qualitate[?] justæ proportionis limites excedente. 2. A virtute formatrice seminibus insita. 3. Vel ex materia redundantia, vel penuria, vel confusione & permixtione. 4. Vel deniq;[?] perversitate subjecti loci.

main_text.head: CAPUT SECUNDUM. DE CORPORUM NATURA-LIUM PRINCIPIIS.
main_text.p: Physicæ partes duæ.PHysicæ partes duæ sunt : COM-MUNIS & PROPRIA. Communis ex Aristotele dici potest quodammodo ACROAMATICA,

page.notes: The printed Latin in the body is transcribed as shown. Doubtful: the mark after "qualitate" and after "diversa" (a printed flourish or reference sign), and "deniq;" (the abbreviation is partly worn). The line "Hysicæ" begins with a large woodcut initial P. The left margin notes read "Monstru." and "Physicæ partes duæ" (the latter spread over three lines in the print). The faint text in the background (show-through from the other side) and the faint "4 3" at the bottom left are not transcribed. No signature is clearly printed.
